source: Abseil's documented library structure: the project is organized as a set of libraries, one per directory under absl/ (base, strings, container, hash, synchronization, time, ...), each a coherent component with its own README/docs on abseil.io.
construction: Each source file under absl/<library>/ is assigned to that <library>. Files outside absl/ (the CMake/ install-test scaffolding) are excluded. 809 files across 21 libraries.
format: RSF `contain absl_<library> <repo-rel-file>` tuples; entities match the file-granularity graph export's node ids.
rater_agreement: GT-exp, single rater. The absl/<dir> = library mapping is the project's own pervasive, documented convention (each absl/ subdir is a distinct library target group), so the assignment is near-mechanical; but because it is a directory-derived expert assertion rather than a published or in-source-declared partition, it is graded GT-exp, not GT-doc. Second rater + kappa deferred (eval §5.3).
caveats: Directory-derived: like ITK, abseil's libraries are directory-aligned, so a naive directory baseline will be competitive — report a2a and cluster count alongside MoJoFM.

Sub-library granularity: abseil splits some libraries into many fine targets (strings -> str_format, cord, cordz_*, ...) that all live under absl/strings/ and so map to one reference library here; the pipeline's target-level containers may be finer or coarser.
